Patterns live HERE, single-sourced (no-magic-values), so modules read them instead of hardcoding. Why browser automation here — is there an official API for this? (a browser is the most expensive/brittle rung.)
Have you checked whether the PDF already has an embedded text layer? OCR is the expensive fallback, not the first step.
Before scraping HTML, is there a sitemap.xml, RSS/Atom feed, or public API/data export? Far cheaper and more stable.
Retry/backoff/circuit-breaker is a solved problem — a mature library (tenacity / resilience4j / polly) likely beats a hand-roll. Why custom?
Mature vector stores exist (qdrant / weaviate / milvus / chroma / pgvector). Building one is high-reinvention — what do they not give you?
Agent/orchestration frameworks already exist (langgraph / crewai / autogen / openai-agents). Is your need really un-served by them?
Auth is the canonical do-not-reinvent (authlib / oauthlib / fastapi-users). Rolling your own is also a security risk — why not adopt one?
Date parsing has brutal edge cases — the stdlib / dateutil / a real lib handle them. What case do they miss?
These signals together suggest you're rebuilding a full auth system — adopt an auth library/provider instead.
Retry + rate-limit + circuit-breaker together = you're rebuilding a resilience layer. A library covers all three.
Normalize + dedupe + ETL together = a data pipeline. A framework (or our own pipeline DAG) likely beats hand-rolling each stage.
Planner + tool-routing + agent-loop together = you're building an orchestration framework that already exists.
